anomalies.observed: On the CAN BUS sheet, the SPI data lines to both MCP2515 controllers are swapped: net CAN_CIPO is wired to pin 14 (S1 = SI, the peripheral data input) of U8 and U9, while net CAN_COPI is wired to pin 15 (S0 = SO, the peripheral data output) of U8 and U9. (The same mis-mapping appears on the SC16IS752 serial chips U13/U14, where SERIAL_CIPO lands on the SI pin and SERIAL_COPI on a non‑SI pin.)
anomalies.expected: Per the spec's own SPI naming note, COPI = 'Controller Out, Peripheral In' (MOSI, master output) and CIPO = 'Controller In, Peripheral Out' (MISO, master input). Therefore CAN_COPI (MOSI) must connect to the MCP2515 SI pin (14) and CAN_CIPO (MISO) must connect to the MCP2515 SO pin (15). The drawing has them reversed.

evidence.quote: CAN BUS sheet: U8 (MCP2515-xSO) pin 14 'S1' -> CAN_CIPO, pin 15 'S0' -> CAN_COPI; U9 (MCP2515-xSO) pin 14 'S1' -> CAN_CIPO, pin 15 'S0' -> CAN_COPI
SPI Naming Note: COPI 'Controller Out, Peripheral In' CIPO 'Controller In, Peripheral Out'

anomalies.impact: The CM4 SPI master's MISO line drives the CAN controllers' data inputs and the controllers' data outputs drive the master's MOSI line. Neither MCP2515 can be configured or polled, so CAN0 and CAN1 are non‑functional; the Odrive motor controllers on J2/J13 cannot be reached.

parsed.summary: The board otherwise matches the spec (16 MHz crystals Y1/Y2, LTC4412 ideal‑diode U6, SM712 TVS D9/D10, SN74LVC1G07 e‑stop buffers U15/U22/U35/U36, WS2812 chain), but the SPI MOSI/MISO nets are swapped onto the wrong pins of both MCP2515 CAN controllers (CAN_CIPO on SI, CAN_COPI on SO), which would disable both CAN buses.
